clue.text: A fine lawn-though it's never mown!

definitions.text: A fine lawn-though it's never mown!

parts.words: A fine lawn-though it's never mown!
parts.note: lawn here is not grass but a fine linen fabric, so it is a cloth that no mower will ever touch

explanation.surface: A gardener admires a beautiful stretch of grass that somehow never needs cutting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lawn' wants to be grass; it is also a fine sheer linen, and this answer is a similar fine white cloth, so of course it is never mown.
explanation.definitionFit: Cambric is a fine, closely woven white linen or cotton fabric, much like the cloth called lawn.

clue.text: Photograph sporting couples

indicators.note: sporting means wearing or showing off, read here as the letters of the next word dressed in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A society photographer snaps pairs of dancers in their finery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sporting' asks for the letters of COUPLES to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A close-up is a photograph taken at short range, filling the frame with its subject.

clue.text: One party got in more money at one time in Portugal

definitions.text: money at one time in Portugal

indicators.note: got in says one piece is taken inside the letters of another word

parts.note: taken as written
one is the Roman numeral I
a do is an informal word for a party

explanation.surface: A single celebration brought in extra cash in old Portugal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'party' is the informal DO, a celebration, not a political group; 'got in' signals the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: The moidore was a gold coin of Portugal, current in the 17th and 18th centuries.

clue.text: A Greek character set about trendy beast

indicators.note: set about means placed around, so one piece surrounds the other

parts.note: rho is a letter of the Greek alphabet
in means fashionable or trendy

explanation.surface: A Greek man attacks a fashionable animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set about' looks like 'attacked', but here signals one piece placed around another.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhino is a short form of rhinoceros, a large horned animal.

clue.text: Frank fed an applicant

parts.note: frank means open and honest, that is candid
fed means ate, as in an animal that fed or ate

explanation.surface: An honest person gave food to a job seeker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fed' reads as feeding someone else; here it means having eaten.
explanation.definitionFit: A candidate is someone who applies or stands for a job or office.

clue.text: Tick immediately available

definitions.meaning: tick is informal for a moment or very short time
describes something ready at once, like quick coffee powder

explanation.surface: A shopper wants something ready the very moment it is asked for.
explanation.definitionFit: A tick is a moment, a very short time; and instant food or coffee is ready for use at once.

clue.text: Isn't rattled about the egghead not being on the level

indicators.note: about here means surrounding, so the rearranged letters go around the other piece
rattled means shaken up, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: the head of egg is its first letter, E

explanation.surface: An intellectual is unflustered when accused of being dishonest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rattled' turns ISNT into INST, and 'about' puts that around E, the first letter (head) of 'egg'.
explanation.definitionFit: An inset panel or piece is set into a surface, so it sits below rather than flush with it.

clue.text: Cash received by an unknown assassin

indicators.note: received by means taken inside, so the first piece goes into the second

parts.note: an unknown person is a stranger
L stands for a pound, from Latin libra, a unit of cash

explanation.surface: Money is paid to a mysterious hired killer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'received by' puts L (pound) inside STRANGER.
explanation.definitionFit: A strangler is one kind of killer, choking the victim.

clue.text: A firedog with 13

parts.note: with means and, joining things together
the answer to 13 across means to iron, as one presses clothes

explanation.surface: A fireplace stand comes along with a cross-reference.
explanation.walkthrough: 13 across means to smooth clothes, so here it gives IRON.
explanation.definitionFit: An andiron is a metal support for logs in a fireplace, also called a firedog.

clue.text: Willing to examine a note

parts.note: to examine is to test
te is a note in tonic sol-fa

explanation.surface: Someone is happy to inspect a memo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Willing' looks like eager, but means having made a will.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who dies testate has left a valid will.

clue.text: View duck taking wing

parts.note: a duck in cricket is a score of nought, the letter O
a pinion is a bird's wing

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher watches a duck taking flight.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a duck is a score of zero, shaped like O.
explanation.definitionFit: An opinion is a view or belief held about something.

clue.text: A holy man goes on horseback or walks

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for saint, a holy man
rides means travels on horseback

explanation.surface: A saint chooses between riding a horse and walking.
explanation.definitionFit: Strides are long steps, so one who strides walks with long paces.

clue.text: Financial expert effecting some difference to incomes

indicators.note: effecting some difference means making a change, here to the order of the letters that follow

explanation.surface: A money adviser changes people's earnings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'effecting some difference' rearranges the letters of TO INCOMES.
explanation.definitionFit: An economist is an expert in the study of money, trade and the economy.

clue.text: Mean with a woman

parts.note: a mean is an average or norm

explanation.surface: Someone stingy is in the company of a lady.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mean' looks like stingy but here is the average, NORM.
explanation.definitionFit: Norma is a female first name.

clue.text: Reporters in force?

definitions.meaning: journalists as a body, the newspaper world
to force, as in ... someone into service

explanation.surface: Journalists turn out in large numbers.
explanation.definitionFit: Journalists collectively are the press, and to press is to force or urge.

clue.text: Pole having a go in the Orient, the outcome is grave

parts.note: S is short for south, a pole of the earth
a go is a turn, as in a game
taken as written
E stands for east, the Orient

explanation.surface: A Polish traveller tries his luck in the East, with a solemn result.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' looks like a Polish man; here it is a geographic pole, S for south.
explanation.definitionFit: Saturnine means gloomy and serious in temperament, so it matches grave.

clue.text: Vehicle adapted for lame Cuban's use

indicators.note: adapted means altered, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: A car is modified for the use of a disabled man from Cuba.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adapted' rearranges LAME CUBAN.
explanation.definitionFit: An ambulance is a vehicle that carries the sick or injured.

clue.text: Toiletry for city sailing men

parts.note: Bath is a city in Somerset, England
salts are experienced sailors

explanation.surface: A bath product is made for urban seamen.
explanation.walkthrough: Bath is a historic English city; old salts are seasoned sailors.
explanation.definitionFit: Bath salts are crystals dissolved in bathwater, a toilet product.

clue.text: Snappy devil, a social worker — has to join in!

parts.note: an imp is a little devil

indicators.note: in tells us the second piece goes inside the first

parts.note: an ant is a social insect, a worker in its colony
to tie is to join together

explanation.surface: A bad-tempered rascal and a welfare officer insist on taking part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a social worker' looks like a welfare officer; it is an insect that lives in a colony. 'in' signals the insertion, and 'has to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An impatient person is irritable and quick to speak sharply.

clue.text: May be sent in with energy, which would be 27 across

indicators.note: may be suggests the letters could be arranged in another way

parts.note: E is the symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: Entries could be submitted with vigour, which shows commitment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'May be' rearranges SENT IN to give INTENS, then E is added.
explanation.definitionFit: Earnest and intense both describe someone very serious and deeply committed.

clue.text: A guide dog

definitions.meaning: something that shows the way or indicates
a breed of gun dog that stands still aiming at game

explanation.surface: A guide dog leads the way.
explanation.definitionFit: A pointer indicates direction, a guide; and the pointer is a hunting breed of dog.

clue.text: Courses for various groups of people

definitions.meaning: as a verb, courses means runs swiftly, or as a noun, contests on a course

explanation.surface: Different lessons are offered to different communities.
explanation.definitionFit: To course is to run fast, as races do; and races are ethnic divisions of humankind.

clue.text: Green after study gives cause to change

indicators.note: after says the first-named piece comes later in the answer

parts.note: to con is to study
vert is green in heraldry

explanation.surface: An environmentalist, after research, gives reason to change.
explanation.walkthrough: VERT is the heraldic word for green.
explanation.definitionFit: To convert is to make something or someone transform into another form or belief.

clue.text: Failing no tests, this is to go ahead

indicators.note: failing means breaking down, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Passing every exam means you may proceed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go ahead' reads as proceed; split it as 'go a head': this hat is worn on one.
explanation.definitionFit: A Stetson is a broad-brimmed hat, something worn on a head.

clue.text: Judge getting a line about 23 down

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the first piece goes around the second

parts.note: a tier is a row or line
the solution to 23 down is abbreviated to the letter R

explanation.surface: A judge gets a row about a cross-reference.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer to 23 down is shortened to R.
explanation.definitionFit: A trier is one who tries a case, that is a judge.

clue.text: Dire scene created in a home

indicators.note: created means made, so the letters are made into something new

explanation.surface: A terrible scene unfolds in a house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'created' rearranges DIRE SCENE.
explanation.definitionFit: A residence is a dwelling, a place where someone lives.

clue.text: Correct title

explanation.surface: A proper heading is required.
explanation.definitionFit: Right means correct; and a right is a legal title or entitlement.

clue.text: Closely follow a well-qualified person's teaching

parts.note: to dog is to follow closely
an MA, Master of Arts, is a well-qualified graduate

explanation.surface: Stick close to a learned scholar's lessons.
explanation.walkthrough: 's' here is just a possessive link; MA is a Master of Arts degree.
explanation.definitionFit: Dogma is a doctrine or set of principles taught as true.

clue.text: Making observations about hospital of little importance

indicators.note: about means around, so the first piece encloses the second

parts.note: noting means observing or remarking

explanation.surface: Doctors' remarks about a hospital are trivial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts H inside NOTING.
explanation.definitionFit: Something described as a nothing affair is trivial and unimportant.

clue.text: Fifty say with minor following-drunk

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty
eg means for example, signalled by say
less means smaller or minor

explanation.surface: A man of fifty with a younger companion staggers home drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' is a common signal for EG, for example.
explanation.definitionFit: Legless is British slang for very drunk, unable to stand.

clue.text: Points put in broadcast aren't sincere

indicators.note: put in says one piece is placed inside the other
broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters are mixed

parts.note: E and S are compass points, east and south

explanation.surface: Insincere remarks are slipped into a radio show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' signals the anagram, which gives EARNT; 'put in' then places the two compass points inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Earnest means serious and heartfelt in intention.

clue.text: Tough guy having a certain skill in bridge

indicators.note: in places the second piece inside the first

parts.note: a span is a bridge or the arch of one
art is a skill or craft

explanation.surface: A strong man shows talent at the card game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bridge' suggests the card game; it is a SPAN across a river.
explanation.definitionFit: A Spartan, from the warlike Greek state, is hardy and austere.
